    'May': 5.73,

    'Dec': 5.47
}

months = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'June', 'July', 'Aug', 'Sept', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec']

# Calculate continuously compounded (log) returns
# r = ln(P_t / P_{t-1})
log_returns = []
for i in range(1, len(months)):
    p_prev = yields[months[i-1]]
    p_curr = yields[months[i]]
    r = math.log(p_curr / p_prev)
    log_returns.append(r)

print(f"\nNumber of log returns: {len(log_returns)}")
print(f"Log returns: {log_returns}")

# Sort returns for percentile calculation
sorted_returns = sorted(log_returns)
print(f"\nSorted returns: {sorted_returns}")

# 5th percentile using nearest-rank method (no interpolation)
# For 5th percentile with n observations: rank = ceil(p * n)
# p = 0.05, n = 11
n = len(log_returns)
rank = math.ceil(0.05 * n)
print(f"\nn = {n}, rank for 5th percentile = ceil(0.05 * {n}) = {rank}")

# The 5th percentile is the rank-th smallest value
percentile_5 = sorted_returns[rank - 1]  # -1 because 0-indexed
print(f"5th percentile (worst) log return: {percentile_5:.6f}")

# Convert to simple percentage (equivalent percentage change in portfolio value)

simple_return = math.exp(percentile_5) - 1
print(f"Simple return equivalent: {simple_return:.6f}")
print(f"Simple return as percentage: {simple_return * 100:.2f}%")

# The VaR as absolute percentage loss
var_percentage = abs(simple_return * 100)
print(f"\nVaR (95% one-month): {var_percentage:.2f}%")

python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# 1996 monthly New Aa municipal bond yields (from Treasury Bulletin Table MY-2)
yields = {
    'Jan': 5.41,
    'Feb': 5.41,
    'Mar': 5.57,
    'Apr': 5.72,
    'May': 5.73,
    'June': 5.82,
    'July': 5.82,
    'Aug': 5.69,
    'Sept': 5.62,
    'Oct': 5.53,
    'Nov': 5.47,
    'Dec': 5.47
}

months = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'June', 'July', 'Aug', 'Sept', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec']

# Calculate month-to-month log returns (continuously compounded)
log_returns = []
for i in range(1, len(months)):
    p_prev = yields[months[i-1]]
    p_curr = yields[months[i]]
    r = math.log(p_curr / p_prev)
    log_returns.append(r)
    print(f"{months[i-1]} -> {months[i]}: {p_prev:.2f}% -> {p_curr:.2f}%, log return: {r:.6f}")

# Sort the returns
sorted_returns = sorted(log_returns)
print(f"\nSorted log returns: {[round(r, 6) for r in sorted_returns]}")

# 5th percentile using nearest-rank method (no interpolation)
# rank = ceil(p * n)
n = len(log_returns)
rank = math.ceil(0.05 * n)
print(f"\nn = {n} monthly returns")
print(f"Rank for 5th percentile = ceil(0.05 × {n}) = ceil({0.05*n}) = {rank}")

# Get the 5th percentile (worst) return
percentile_5 = sorted_returns[rank - 1]
print(f"5th percentile (worst) log return: {percentile_5:.6f}")

# Convert to simple percentage change
# Simple return = exp(log_return) - 1
simple_return = math.exp(percentile_5) - 1
print(f"Simple return = exp({percentile_5:.6f}) - 1 = {simple_return:.6f}")

# VaR as absolute percentage loss
var_percentage = round(abs(simple_return) * 100, 2)
print(f"\n95% one-month VaR = {var_percentage}%")

# Write to file
with open('/app/answer.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(str(var_percentage))

print(f"\nAnswer written to /app/answer.txt: {var_percentage}%")
EOF
